rules.text: Deadpan, never cringe
No HR or corporate music: beds 88-100 BPM, minor, minimal, no hooks or build-ups. A bed you approved in your music ledger passes: your yes is the measure this proxy stands in for
The bed is a media-library music entry or a track in your music ledger's `approved`; never a motion_score render

Every bed's file (by sha256) is in your music ledger's `approved`: your own yes for the track, or a bed made for this film (`approved_by: "made for this film"` and `film`; it counts for that film only), judged by ear in the render; a bed you rejected fails with your words even when it is also approved
Under the narration the bed sits at least 12 LU below the voice, measured on the voice and music stems
Under every meme that plays its own sound the bed ducks at least 6 dB below its level under the narration, or is silent
Under every meme that plays its own sound the bed sits at least 18 LU below the meme's line, or is silent, so the line plays clear
No vocals in a bed: silero VAD finds a voice in under 5% of the track (instrumental beds measured 0%, a sung track 85%)
No text walls: >=12 unspoken on-screen words under a different sentence
Real X/Reddit posts and real people, captured with source and date
Nothing important in the 10% edge band
No cut-off text: in every held state of a picture, no visible word or captured page line is cut by a card, a window, the stage or the frame
Tags, stickers and chips never lie over other text: in every held state, none covers more than 10% of a visible word or page line
No end card; credits go in the YouTube description
No lower thirds everywhere: a source label shows once, small, about 2 s
No Fireship footage or mention
Every source at least 720p
A meme plays its whole spoken line, setup included, cut on silence in the clip source; a payoff word alone is not a meme
No film, show, game or creator supplies more than one meme in a film; a callback reusing the same asset counts once, and so does one meme row played in parts
No credit or source tag on a meme; credits go in the description
No captioned meme grids
The narration is cut only in silence, never on live speech

Every take the cut plays is the brand's voice, one {voiceId, modelId} pair for the whole cut, recorded per take in voice/jobs.json: the pair the brand kit declares in <brand>/brand/voice.json, else the default voice in Settings (Media generation). A take on another voice or model fails, naming the take, and a cut that mixes pairs fails; with no brand voice and no Settings default, or a take with no recorded pair, the rule is unchecked, so the cut blocks. A film never changes the voice model to fit time: another model makes a cloned voice sound like someone else; fix length in the script
No sound effect over a narration word
A meme stops the narration only at a sentence end
No 1 s run without narration or sound near voice level

Show, don't tell: while the narration speaks, the picture changes at least every 5 s (a new picture, a motion-graphic reveal, a meme or clip). A sticker or label is not a change. A page shown as a receipt holds at most 4 s before something explains it

A motion-graphic scene never snaps back to a frame it already showed: a scene the next line keeps continues from its settled state instead of rebuilding from scratch. Measured on the render; 1 s or more fails
The cold open lands its first meme or punch within 4 s
A written statement is never voiced as a question: the render's transcript ends no statement with a question mark
No blank screen: never 1.5 s or more of an empty stage or a motion-graphic title with nothing revealed yet
An extended analogy (the spine's anchor_world) is shown as a motion-graphic scene that acts it out, never one still photo
Deadpan never labels its own joke: no 'that part is our joke', 'just kidding', 'joking aside'. A fairness caveat is stated plainly as a fact
A meme voices what the target audience feels at that moment, not what the subject or the narrator feels: 'nice' over an 80% margin is the subject's reaction, not the viewer's

rules.text: A meme template is used in its most widely recognised version: its library entry's canonical.is is true, from evidence (library_tag canonical {is, basis}, the Know Your Meme page or most-viewed upload) or your switch on the Library page; an entry without canonical fails
Every meme lands something the narration just set up; a viewer can say why it is there. No meme as decoration

rules.text: The film's analogy (spine anchor_world) is acted out only in the world it sets up: its objects never wander into a new setting or story the analogy and the narration never named. Judged per narrator line on the frames-only reader's description: kit g11plan.seen_judged at K-9.
